sentences.text:
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition Nos.6468 and 6631 of 2012
Common Order:
Since the issue involved in both the Writ Petitions is one and the same, they are being disposed of by this common order.

2. Heard Sri B.Narayana Reddy, learned Senior Counsel for Sri Sanjeev Gillela, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondents, and perused the record.
3.

Shorn of unnecessary details, it is the common case of the petitioners in both the Writ Petitions is that, aggrieved by the Land Acquisition Award dated 03-08-1994, they along with other land losers have approached respondent No.3 authority and submitted application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') seeking reference of the Award to Court for proper determination of the compensation payable

, and in spite of the petitioners submitting the aforementioned application under Section 18 of the Act, the same has not been referred to the Court by respondent No.3 till date, which action it is contended as highly illegal and arbitrary and contrary to the scheme of the Act.
4. Counter-affidavit on behalf of respondents is filed.
5. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition by referring to the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of the respondents would contend that since the petitioners did not submit individual applications seeking reference to the Court under Section 18 of the Act, the said application has not been considered by the respondent authorities.
6. Learned Government Pleader further submits that the petitioners having received compensation under the Award on 30-08-1994 had filed the application under Section 18 of the Act along with others on the same day and for the said reason also, petitioners are not entitled to seek reference under Section 18 of the Act.
7.

Learned Government Pleader also submits that the petitioners instead of submitting application under Section 18 of the Act individually, have submitted joint application along with 20 others under Section 18 of the Act, and thus, the action of the respondent authorities in not referring the application to Court is justified.

sentences.text: I have taken note of respective contentions urged.

9. The petitioners' claim that though the respondents have determined the compensation payable in respect of their properties acquired by the Award dated 03-08-1994, the petitioners while receiving the compensation amount on 30-08-1994 having recoded their protest to the same by submitting an application to respondent No.3 under Section 18 of the Act, the respondent authorities are required to make a reference of the said application to the Court for proper determination of the compensation.

10. Further, it is also to be noted that the second proviso to section 31 of the Act also stipulates that a person receiving the compensation under protest shall be entitled to make an application under Section 18 of the Act, and inasmuch as the petitioners while receiving compensation having recorded their protest, are entitled to file application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference to the Court.

11. Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ajit Singh v/s. State of Punjab 1 also having held that the filing of application under Section 18 of the Act itself is to be considered as an implied protest (1994)
4 SCC 67 and mere receiving of compensation would not come in the way of the authority in considering the said application, this Court is of the view that the action of the respondent No.3 authority in not referring the application filed by the petitioners along with co- claimants to the Court cannot be held to be valid.

entities.text: Ajit Singh v/s. State of Punjab 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Accordingly, respondent No.3 authority is directed to make reference of the application filed by the petitioners along with 20 other as co-claimants under the Award dated 03-08-1994 to the concerned Court of Civil Jurisdiction within a period of six (06) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
13. Subject to above direction, the Writ Petitions are disposed of.
14. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.

_ T. VINOD KUMAR, J Date : 11-11-2024 Vsv Bolla Anji Reddy vs The Government Of Andhra Pradesh, on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73038424/
